Pentecost (Doctrine)
PEN-tih-kost
n.
From Greek pentēkostē, “fiftieth,” counted from the day after the Passover Sabbath as the fiftieth day of the firstfruits-counting; the OT Feast of Weeks (Hebrew chag shavū‘ot) and the day of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the church (Acts 2).

📖 Biblical Definition

Pentecost is the great spring harvest festival of Israel and the day on which the Holy Spirit was poured out upon the New Testament church in fulfillment of Christ’s promise. Both meanings stand together in the Bible, the second fulfilling the first. The OT institution prescribed in Leviticus 23:15-21 commanded Israel to count seven complete weeks from the day after the Passover Sabbath (the day of the wave-offering of the firstfruits of the barley harvest), and on the fiftieth day to observe the Feast of Weeks (Hebrew chag shavū‘ot; Greek pentēkostē, fiftieth). Two loaves of leavened wheat bread were waved before the LORD, with sacrifices of seven lambs, one bullock, and two rams as burnt offerings, plus a kid for a sin offering and two lambs of the first year for a peace offering. The Feast of Weeks therefore celebrated the wheat harvest (the second great harvest of the year) and (in later Jewish tradition) the giving of the Law at Sinai, which was reckoned as having occurred fifty days after the Exodus. The New Testament fulfillment is on the day of Pentecost in Acts 2. The disciples, gathered in Jerusalem as Christ had instructed (Acts 1:4), are filled with the Holy Spirit; cloven tongues like as of fire sit upon each of them; they speak with other tongues as the Spirit gives them utterance; Peter preaches the great Pentecost sermon, the church receives the Spirit publicly, and three thousand souls are baptized into the church that day. The structural significance is enormous. First, the timing: the outpouring of the Spirit at Pentecost is theologically meaningful because the day was already the day of the wheat harvest’s firstfruits. The three thousand souls baptized at Pentecost are the firstfruits of the great gospel-harvest now beginning; James later calls believers a kind of firstfruits of his creatures (Jas 1:18). Second, the universalizing direction: the cloven tongues prefigure the going-forth of the gospel to every tongue and nation; the very list of nations in Acts 2:9-11 sets the missionary trajectory. Third, the new covenant inauguration: the Spirit’s indwelling of the church marks the formal arrival of the new covenant promised by the prophets (Jer 31:31-34; Ezek 36:26-27) in which the Spirit is poured out, the law written on hearts, and God’s people made one across every natural division. Fourth, the typological fulfillment: the OT Feast of Weeks anticipated the Day of Pentecost; the wheat-harvest firstfruits anticipated the Spirit-harvest firstfruits of three thousand souls; the giving of the Law at Sinai (in later Jewish tradition) is set against the giving of the Spirit at Pentecost (in the apostolic record). Pentecost is therefore the birthday of the New Covenant church in its Spirit-filled public manifestation, with the Spirit poured out upon all flesh in fulfillment of Joel 2:28-32, which Peter quotes in his sermon.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines PENTECOST as a solemn festival of the Jews; so called because celebrated on the fiftieth day from the second day of the passover; also, the day on which the Holy Ghost descended upon the apostles, fulfilling the type of the OT Feast of Weeks.

expand to see more

PENTECOST, n. — 1. A solemn festival of the Jews; so called because celebrated on the fiftieth day from the second day of the passover, which was the sixteenth of the month Nisan. The first day was set apart for receiving the sheaf of barley; on the morrow, the priest waved the sheaf before the LORD. From this day was reckoned the fiftieth, called the Feast of Weeks, or Pentecost. 2. Whitsuntide; the day on which the Holy Ghost descended upon the apostles, in fulfillment of the type of the OT Feast of Weeks (Acts 2).

📖 Key Scripture

Acts 2:1-4 — "And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance."

Leviticus 23:15-16 — "And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete: Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the LORD."

Acts 2:16-17 — "But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel; And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh..."

1 Corinthians 16:8 — "But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Pentecost is corrupted, on one side, by the disconnection of NT Pentecost from its OT typological roots (so that the Spirit’s outpouring is preached without the wheat-harvest firstfruits and Feast-of-Weeks substance the day already carried)—and on the other by the Pentecostal-traditions corruption that has treated Acts 2 as the normative template for ongoing personal Spirit-baptism experiences, against the apostolic doctrine that the once-for-all Pentecostal outpouring constituted the church and continues by indwelling rather than by repeated reception.

expand to see more

The disconnection of NT Pentecost from its OT typological roots is the more general contemporary corruption. The Spirit’s outpouring at Pentecost is preached without the wheat-harvest firstfruits substance, without the Feast-of-Weeks fiftieth-day-counting context, without the giving-of-the-Law-at-Sinai parallel that fills out the typology. The result is a Pentecost that hangs loose in Christian preaching, a one-time historical event with no rich OT substructure. The recovery is the recovery of the typology. Christ rose on the day after the Passover Sabbath (which was the day of the wave-offering of the firstfruits of barley); fifty days later, on the day already celebrated as the Feast of Weeks and the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, the Spirit was poured out and three thousand souls baptized as the firstfruits of the new covenant ingathering. The typological precision is the apostolic intent.

The opposite corruption is the Pentecostal-traditions reading of Acts 2 as the normative template for ongoing personal Spirit-baptism experiences—treating the day’s phenomena (tongues, fire, rushing wind) as the standard pattern by which every believer should experience subsequent Spirit-baptisms after conversion. The apostolic doctrine reads Acts 2 differently. The Pentecostal outpouring was the once-for-all constituting event by which the Spirit was given to the church as a body; subsequent believers receive the same Spirit at conversion through union with Christ (1 Cor 12:13, for by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body); the phenomena of Acts 2 are not normative for ongoing repeated experiences but constitutive of the church’s foundational reception of the Spirit. The continuing ministry of the Spirit is the indwelling, sealing, sanctifying, gifting work He performs in every believer from conversion onward, not a series of repeated Pentecost-style experiences. Recover both ends. Restore the OT typological substance of Pentecost (against the disconnection), and refuse the Pentecostal-traditions reading that turns the foundational event into a normative template (against the over-extension). The biblical Pentecost is the once-for-all outpouring that constituted the church; the Spirit continues His full ministry through indwelling, gifting, and applying to every believer the redemption Christ accomplished.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek pentēkostē (fiftieth); Hebrew chag shavū‘ot (Feast of Weeks); the OT spring harvest festival on the fiftieth day from the firstfruits of barley, fulfilled in the NT day of Pentecost (Acts 2) when the Spirit was poured out upon the church as the firstfruits of the new covenant ingathering.

expand to see more

Greek pentēkostē (G4005) — fiftieth, Pentecost (3 NT uses: Acts 2:1; 20:16; 1 Cor 16:8).

Hebrew chag shavū‘ot — Feast of Weeks (Ex 34:22; Deut 16:10).

Hebrew shavūa‘ (H7620) — week (the singular of shavū‘ot).

Joel 2:28-32 — the prophetic basis of Pentecost (Peter quotes it as fulfilled in Acts 2:17-21).

"When the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place—Acts 2 sets the day of the Spirit’s outpouring on the day of the OT Feast of Weeks."

"The three thousand souls baptized at Pentecost are the firstfruits of the new covenant gospel-harvest, fulfilling the OT firstfruits of the wheat harvest."

"Disconnection from OT roots loses the typological substance; Pentecostal-traditions reading turns the foundational event into a normative template for repeated experiences; biblical Pentecost is the once-for-all constituting outpouring fulfilling Joel 2 and the Feast of Weeks."
